decisions.reason: A classic door lever handle close to the core range carries little extra cost to keep and has a long life cycle in architectural hardware.
Handle families are system offerings that architects specify across projects, so withdrawing one a year after launch would be unusual.
A new handle design fits the firm's design-led positioning and needs time for specification cycles to build demand.
This core-range design product is cheap to maintain alongside existing production, and handle lines are typically kept for many years.
A lever handle family supports the broad system offering and integrates with existing fittings, so it should be kept.
The L700 electronic access system with its unique light technology matches the strategic push into digital building organization and is likely to be developed further.
